actions.name: PHQ-9 depression screen (administered)
actions.result: Score 14/27 (moderate depression). See item-level detail in attached PHQ-9 form. Denies intent or plan when screened; endorses passive wish not to wake up some mornings.

actions.name: Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) screening
actions.result: Structured screen: passive ideation present ('no use to anybody'), denies active plan, denies intent, denies prior attempts, denies current preparatory behavior. Separate interview observation (not part of C-SSRS scoring): when asked directly about access to lethal means, patient was initially evasive and changed the subject before disclosing further.

actions.name: Home safety and environment review via camera
actions.result: Camera pan shows cluttered single-wide trailer, space heater in use, patient wearing winter coat and gloves indoors, thermostat reportedly set low 'to save money,' minimal furniture, no visible smoke detector chirp/test button response when asked, pathway to door partially blocked by boxes.

actions.name: Nutritional/food security screen (Hunger Vital Sign)
actions.result: Patient reports 'the food just doesn't last' and worries food will run out before more money comes most months; refrigerator shown on camera contains minimal perishable food, mostly condiments and a few canned goods.

actions.name: Financial exploitation screening (capacity-based interview)
actions.result: Patient demonstrates intact orientation and reasoning about his finances; recalls his pension amount and due dates accurately; able to describe the general arrangement that his nephew holds his bank card. No impairment in reasoning or recall identified on this capacity-focused screen.

actions.name: Fall risk and functional mobility self-report
actions.result: Patient reports he can get from bed to recliner and to the bathroom holding furniture, uses a cane inconsistently, has not started home exercises recommended at discharge, reports pain '6 out of 10' with deep breaths or movement.

actions.name: Decision-making capacity screen (social work bedside assessment)
actions.result: Patient is alert and oriented x4, articulates understanding of his living situation and financial arrangement, and expresses his preferences consistently and coherently across the interview. On this brief conversational screen, the social worker's clinical impression is that there is no obvious evidence of cognitive impairment; this is not a formal capacity determination and would require further evaluation if a legal determination were needed.

actions.name: Social support and isolation assessment
actions.result: Patient reports he used to attend a weekly veterans' breakfast at the VFW hall but has not gone in about two months; names one neighbor who checks in 'now and then' but no regular daily contact; nephew Dale is primary contact.

actions.name: Review hospital discharge summary
actions.result: Discharged 7 days ago after fall at home with closed fractures of ribs 6-8, managed conservatively with pain control; patient declined subacute rehab placement and physical therapy follow-up, discharged home with instructions for incentive spirometry, pain management, and outpatient PCP follow-up in 2 weeks. Discharge documentation notes 'patient lives alone, limited support confirmed by patient at time of discharge.'

actions.name: Review current medication list
actions.result: Acetaminophen 650mg PO q6h PRN pain, Lisinopril 10mg daily, Atorvastatin 20mg nightly. Pharmacy refill history shows acetaminophen and lisinopril refilled on schedule; atorvastatin refill is 45 days overdue.

actions.name: Review veterans' benefits enrollment status
actions.result: VA record shows patient is enrolled in VA healthcare (Priority Group 3, service-connected hearing loss rated 10%), but has no record of VA Aid & Attendance pension benefit application or current VA Homemaker/Home Health Aide services; no record of referral to VA caregiver support program.

actions.name: Review prior social work note from 6 months ago
actions.result: Prior outpatient social work contact (6 months ago, unrelated ED visit) noted patient 'reports managing independently, nephew assists with errands,' no concerns documented at that time regarding finances or safety.

actions.name: Review local Area Agency on Aging / APS intake requirements (West Virginia)
actions.result: West Virginia DHHR Adult Protective Services accepts reports of suspected financial exploitation and self-neglect of vulnerable adults; mandated reporters must report regardless of the adult's capacity to make decisions when exploitation or neglect is suspected; report can be made by phone or online with case details.

facts.chart: Veteran discharged 7 days ago after fall with rib fractures; declined rehab facility; hospital social work follow-up call.
facts.says: They said somebody would call to check on me after I fell and busted up my ribs. I'm managing. I didn't want to go to one of them facilities.

facts.chart: Patient reports fall occurred at home, mechanism unclear, found self on floor, called neighbor for help.
facts.says: I don't rightly know how I ended up on the floor. Just went down. My neighbor Russell found me a while after and called the ambulance.

facts.chart: Reports ongoing rib pain 6/10 with movement and deep breathing, one week post-injury.
facts.says: Breathing deep still hurts something awful. Hurts to get up out of the chair too.

facts.chart: Lives alone in single-wide trailer outside Beckley, WV; longtime residence.
facts.says: Been in this trailer going on twenty years now. Just me since my wife passed.

facts.chart: Reports keeping thermostat low to conserve money; wearing coat indoors during visit.
facts.says: I keep it turned down low. Got my coat on, I'm alright.

facts.chart: Reports electric company nearly disconnected service last month due to unpaid balance.
facts.says: Power company sent a letter saying they'd cut it off. Dale said he took care of it but I don't know.

facts.chart: Nephew Dale manages patient's finances and holds his bank card; arrangement patient describes as having 'no choice.'
facts.says: Dale handles the money now. Took my card a while back, said it'd be easier that way, me not getting around so good.

facts.chart: Patient reports his pension income has been decreasing/disappearing without clear explanation; reluctant to question nephew.
facts.says: My pension check comes in but by the time I ask for some, there ain't much left. I don't like to ask too many questions.

facts.chart: Reports nephew becomes angry when patient asks about money; patient avoids confrontation out of fear of losing help.
facts.says: Dale gets awful short with me if I bring it up. I don't want to make him mad, he's all the family I got close by.

facts.chart: Patient fears that disclosing financial concerns will lead to nephew's arrest or to patient being placed in a facility against his will.
facts.says: I don't want Dale getting in trouble. And I sure don't want nobody putting me in one of them homes. I'd rather just manage.

facts.chart: Reports minimal food supply; running low before next income arrives; skipping meals some days.
facts.says: Food gets thin toward the end of the month. I been skipping breakfast some days, just have coffee.

facts.chart: No longer drives; relies on nephew for grocery trips, which have become infrequent.
facts.says: I don't drive no more since my eyes got bad. Dale's supposed to bring groceries but it's been slim lately.

facts.chart: Stopped attending weekly veterans' breakfast at VFW hall approximately 2 months ago.
facts.says: Used to go every Thursday to the VFW for breakfast with the fellas. Haven't been in a couple months now.

facts.chart: Reports lacking transportation and low motivation/energy as reasons for stopping breakfast attendance.
facts.says: No real way to get there anymore, and honestly I just ain't had it in me to go.

facts.chart: Reports persistent low mood, hopelessness, and anhedonia over past 2 months, worsened since the fall.
facts.says: I've been down a long while now. Since the fall it's been worse. Hard to see much point some days.

facts.chart: Patient states flatly he feels he is 'no use to anybody' when discussing his situation.
facts.says: Honest truth, I ain't no use to anybody no more. Can't work, can't hardly help myself.

facts.chart: Reports keeping a loaded rifle by the front door, states it is for home protection.
facts.says: I keep my rifle by the door, loaded. Always have, for protection out here.

facts.chart: Denies active suicidal plan or intent when asked directly; endorses passive thoughts of not minding if he didn't wake up.
facts.says: I ain't going to do nothing to myself. But some mornings I wake up and think, well, wouldn't matter much if I hadn't.

facts.chart: Reports hope of seeing grandchildren, faith community ties, and reluctance to burden others as reasons against self-harm.
facts.says: I got grandkids I'd like to see grow up. And my church, Pastor Combs checks on me some. I wouldn't want to put nobody out.

facts.chart: US Army veteran; served in his twenties; retired long-distance lineman after military service.
facts.says: Served my time in the Army when I was young, then worked thirty-some years as a lineman, long-distance lines.

facts.chart: Reports hearing loss, service-connected, uses hearing aids inconsistently.
facts.says: My hearing's not what it was from all them years on the lines. Got hearing aids but the batteries cost money so I don't always wear 'em.

facts.chart: Reports using furniture and walls for support getting around trailer; cane used inconsistently; has not started discharge home exercises.
facts.says: I kind of make my way holding onto things. Got a cane somewhere but I don't always use it.

facts.chart: Reports taking pain reliever and blood pressure pill regularly; uncertain about cholesterol medication refill status.
facts.says: I take my pain pills and my blood pressure pill. The other one, the cholesterol one, I think I'm about out.

facts.chart: Declined inpatient rehab facility placement at discharge; wanted to return home.
facts.says: They wanted to send me to one of them rehab places. I told them no, I wanted to come home.

facts.chart: One neighbor, Russell, checks in occasionally but not daily; no formal home care services in place.
facts.says: Russell next door looks in on me now and again, not every day though.

facts.chart: Patient reports nephew Dale has his own financial difficulties and recently lost a job.
facts.says: Dale's had it rough too, lost his job a few months back. I reckon that's partly why he's been short on patience.

facts.chart: Patient expresses strong fear of being placed in a nursing facility or losing independence if he discloses difficulties.
facts.says: I'd rather just tough it out than have somebody come put me in a home. I been independent my whole life.

facts.chart: Reports decreased appetite and early morning waking over past 2 months; denies significant weight change he is aware of.
facts.says: I don't eat much some days, and I wake up real early, can't get back to sleep. Don't know if I've lost weight, don't have a scale.

facts.chart: Denies current alcohol use; reports quit drinking approximately 15 years ago.
facts.says: I don't drink no more. Quit that about fifteen years back.

facts.chart: No personal vehicle access; relies entirely on nephew or neighbor for transportation to appointments and errands.
facts.says: I don't have no way to get around myself. Depend on Dale or Russell.

facts.chart: States he wants to stay in his own home, keep his independence, and does not want anyone 'in trouble' - open to help that does not involve moving out or involving police with his nephew.
facts.says: I just want to stay right here in my own place. If you can help without stirring up trouble for Dale or getting me hauled off somewhere, I'd be grateful.

facts.chart: History of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both long-standing and previously well-controlled.
facts.says: I got the high blood pressure and the cholesterol thing, had those a long while.

facts.chart: Wife passed away approximately 5 years ago; patient reports this as a significant loss.
facts.says: Lost my wife about five years back. Was married forty-two years. Still feels strange being here without her.

artifacts.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
artifacts.author: Beckley Regional Hospital, Hospitalist Service
artifacts.body: 79-year-old male admitted after a fall at home resulting in closed fractures of ribs 6, 7, and 8 on the right. Managed conservatively with oral analgesia and incentive spirometry. Hospital course uncomplicated. Patient was offered placement at a subacute rehabilitation facility for strengthening and monitoring; patient declined and expressed strong preference to return home. Discharged home after 3-day stay with instructions for pain management, incentive spirometry use, activity as tolerated, and outpatient PCP follow-up in 2 weeks. At time of discharge, patient reported living alone with 'limited support confirmed by patient.' Social work referral placed for post-discharge psychosocial follow-up given solo living situation and recent fall.

cells: Every 6 hours as needed for pain

artifacts.title: Prior Outpatient Social Work Contact Note
artifacts.author: Beckley Regional Hospital, Social Work (ED consult)
artifacts.body: Brief social work contact during unrelated ED visit for minor laceration. Patient reported managing independently at home, stated nephew 'helps with errands.' No concerns raised at that time regarding financial management, food access, home safety, or mood. No further social work follow-up recommended at that visit.

artifacts.title: PHQ-9 Depression Screening Result
artifacts.author: Social Work, current telehealth visit
artifacts.body: Total score: 14/27 (moderate depression range). Item-level notable responses: 'Little interest or pleasure in doing things' - several days; 'Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless' - nearly every day; 'Trouble falling/staying asleep or sleeping too much' - nearly every day (early waking); 'Poor appetite or overeating' - several days (poor appetite); 'Thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself' - several days (score 1). No endorsement of a specific plan or intent on follow-up questioning.

artifacts.title: VA Benefits and Enrollment Summary
artifacts.author: VA Medical Center, Beckley VAMC (record extract)
artifacts.body: Veteran status confirmed: US Army, honorable discharge. Enrolled in VA healthcare, Priority Group 3, service-connected disability rating 10% for bilateral hearing loss. No record of application for VA Aid & Attendance pension benefit (enhanced monthly pension for veterans needing assistance with daily activities). No current enrollment in VA Homemaker/Home Health Aide program. No referral on file to VA Caregiver Support Program. Veteran last used VA primary care services approximately 14 months ago.

artifacts.title: West Virginia Adult Protective Services - Mandated Reporter Guidance (excerpt)
artifacts.author: WV Department of Health and Human Resources, Bureau for Social Services
artifacts.body: Any person who has reasonable cause to believe that an incapacitated or vulnerable adult is being abused, neglected, or financially exploited shall report such belief to the Department. Reports may be made regardless of the adult's capacity to make decisions, including when the adult has decision-making capacity but is nonetheless at risk due to exploitation, undue influence, or inability or unwillingness to protect themselves. Reporter identity may be kept confidential. Reports can be made via the toll-free hotline or online portal and should include the adult's name, address, nature of concern, and any known responsible party.

objectives.text: Build rapport sufficient to elicit reluctant/hidden disclosures about financial exploitation, fear of consequences, and firearm access, demonstrating trust-building and trauma-informed interviewing.
Conduct a thorough suicide risk assessment distinguishing passive ideation from active intent/plan, and elicit firearm access as a lethality factor through direct, sensitive follow-up questioning.

Assess self-neglect indicators (home environment, heat, food insecurity, medication/mobility management) and financial exploitation indicators, synthesizing findings into a biopsychosocial formulation.

Correctly determine and articulate the duty to report suspected financial exploitation/self-neglect to Adult Protective Services even though the patient has intact decision-making capacity and does not want a report made.

Identify and connect the veteran to appropriate concrete resources (VA Aid & Attendance pension, VA Homemaker/Home Health Aide or caregiver support, local food assistance/Meals on Wheels, veterans' service organization transportation) within social work scope, rather than attempting clinical management.

Recognize and reflect on a patient-chart mismatch (prior social work note found no concerns six months ago vs. current significant findings) to understand how exploitation/neglect can escalate or go undetected, and the overdue statin refill as a secondary adherence concern not central to the main safety issue.

answerKey.primaryProblem: Suspected financial exploitation of a vulnerable older adult (by nephew/caregiver) with associated self-neglect (inadequate heat, food insecurity, medication gaps) and comorbid moderate depression with passive suicidal ideation in the context of access to a firearm, occurring after a recent fall-related hospitalization in a patient who retains decision-making capacity.
differential: Financial exploitation by a family member/caregiver with coercive control dynamics
Self-neglect (independent of exploitation) due to functional decline, isolation, and depression
Major depressive episode, moderate severity, with passive suicidal ideation, precipitated/worsened by injury, pain, isolation, and loss of role
Normal grief/adjustment reaction to aging and loss of independence without clinical depression (less likely given duration, pervasiveness, and PHQ-9 score)
Caregiver strain/burnout in nephew rather than intentional exploitation (consider but does not negate reporting duty or safety concerns)
keyFindings: Cold, cluttered home; patient wearing coat indoors; near utility disconnection last month
Minimal food in home, reports skipping meals, no reliable transportation for groceries
Nephew Dale controls bank card and pension funds; patient reports money 'disappearing,' fears asking questions, fears nephew getting in trouble or himself being institutionalized if he discloses
PHQ-9 = 14 (moderate depression); passive suicidal ideation ('wouldn't matter much if I hadn't woken up'); denies active plan/intent
Loaded rifle kept by front door — important lethality/means consideration despite denial of intent
Stopped attending veterans' breakfast ~2 months ago; increasing isolation
Decision-making capacity intact on bedside screen

Mismatch: prior social work note 6 months ago found 'no concerns' with same nephew arrangement, contrasting with current significant findings — exploitation/neglect may be progressive or was previously underdetected
Atorvastatin refill 45 days overdue despite patient reporting he takes 'the other one' — mild adherence gap, secondary to primary safety concerns
No VA Aid & Attendance application on file; not enrolled in VA Homemaker/Home Health Aide despite apparent need
plan: Conduct and document full suicide risk assessment (completed: PHQ-9, C-SSRS); given passive ideation plus firearm access, implement lethality means-safety counseling - discuss safe storage/temporary removal or securing of firearm with patient and, with consent, a trusted third party; provide crisis line number (988) and safety plan; this is within social work scope and does not require psychiatric hospitalization given capacity, no active plan/intent, and presence of protective factors, but warrants close follow-up and likely referral to outpatient behavioral health/VA mental health services

File a mandated report to West Virginia Adult Protective Services regarding suspected financial exploitation and self-neglect; this duty applies even though patient has decision-making capacity and does not want a report made - explain this honestly and compassionately to the patient before or at the time of filing, emphasizing APS's role is protective, not punitive, and that reporting is a legal duty, not a betrayal

Explore with patient, in a non-confrontational way, options for safer financial oversight (e.g., VA fiduciary program, trusted secondary contact, bank alerts) rather than framing it as removing all of Dale's involvement, to reduce patient's fear and resistance
Refer/connect to VA Aid & Attendance pension benefit application and VA Homemaker/Home Health Aide or Caregiver Support Program via VA social work/benefits counselor
Connect to local food resources: Meals on Wheels of Raleigh County, local VFW/American Legion food pantry, and SNAP eligibility screening
Coordinate transportation options for VFW veterans' breakfast and medical appointments (VSO van, Area Agency on Aging transportation) to reduce isolation
Communicate medical findings (overdue statin refill, deconditioning, unaddressed fall risk) back to PCP/discharge team for medical follow-up - outside social work scope to manage medications directly
Schedule close follow-up contact (within 1 week) to reassess mood, safety, and whether APS/VA referrals have been initiated, and to continue trust-building
redFlags: Passive suicidal ideation with access to a loaded firearm
Suspected ongoing financial exploitation by a family member in a position of trust
Signs of self-neglect including inadequate heating and food insecurity in a recently hospitalized, physically compromised older adult
Patient's fear of retaliation or involuntary placement, which may suppress future disclosure and requires reporting regardless
educationPoints: Decision-making capacity does not exempt a social worker from mandated reporting duties when financial exploitation or self-neglect of a vulnerable adult is suspected; capacity and the duty to report operate on separate tracks.

Passive suicidal ideation combined with firearm access is a meaningful lethality consideration even without an expressed plan or intent; means-safety counseling is a core social work safety intervention.

Financial exploitation by family caregivers often coexists with genuine affection and caregiver strain; reporting is about protecting the older adult, not necessarily punishing the family member, and this framing can be used to reduce patient resistance.
Self-neglect and exploitation can be subtle and may not surface in a single prior encounter (as seen in the 6-month-old note); longitudinal and trust-based assessment is often required to detect it.

Veterans with service-connected benefits may be under-enrolled in supportive VA programs (Aid & Attendance, Homemaker/Home Health Aide, Caregiver Support); proactive benefits navigation is squarely within social work scope.
Respecting a patient's stated goals (staying in his own home, not wanting the nephew 'in trouble') should shape how options are presented, without compromising mandatory reporting obligations.

patient.name: Clarence Boyd
patient.occupation: Retired long-distance lineman; US Army veteran
patient.appearance: An older man with thinning white hair and a weathered, deeply lined face is seated in a worn recliner, wearing a heavy canvas coat zipped up indoors. The room behind him is dim and cluttered with stacked boxes and a space heater visible in frame; his affect is flat and tired, with brief moments of tearfulness when certain topics come up.

persona.personality: Proud, stoic, self-reliant by habit, with a dry quiet humor that surfaces occasionally; ashamed of his current circumstances and reluctant to appear needy.
persona.communicationStyle: Speaks slowly and plainly in short sentences, Appalachian regional phrasing, tends to minimize problems and deflect with 'I'm managing' until trust is built; becomes more open with gentle, patient, non-judgmental questioning.
persona.emotionalState: Fatigued, low mood, guarded, intermittently tearful; anxious specifically about being institutionalized or having Dale 'get in trouble.'
persona.background: Grew up in rural West Virginia, served in the US Army in his twenties, then spent over three decades as a long-distance lineman climbing poles across the region. Married for 42 years before his wife passed about five years ago; one nephew, Dale, is his closest nearby family. Used to enjoy fixing small engines and attending the weekly veterans' breakfast at the VFW hall before he stopped going a couple of months ago.
speechExamples: I'm managing, I don't want to be no bother.
Dale's a good boy, he's just had it rough lately.
I been independent my whole life, don't aim to stop now.
Honest truth, some mornings I don't much care if I wake up or not.
I'd rather tough it out than get hauled off somewhere.
concerns: Being placed in a nursing home or assisted living against his will
Getting his nephew Dale 'in trouble' with the law
Running out of money or food before the next check comes
Being seen as unable to manage on his own after the fall

scenario.studentBrief: You are a social work student conducting a telehealth follow-up video visit for Clarence Boyd, a 79-year-old veteran who was discharged one week ago after a fall resulting in rib fractures. He declined rehab placement and lives alone. The inpatient team has asked social work to follow up given his solo living situation.
scenario.chiefComplaint: Post-discharge psychosocial follow-up after fall with rib fractures in an older veteran living alone
scenario.openingLine: They said somebody would call to check on me after I fell and busted up my ribs. I'm managing. I didn't want to go to one of them facilities.
tasks: Build rapport and conduct a biopsychosocial assessment of the home situation
Screen for depression and suicide risk, including access to means
Assess for adequacy of food, heat, medications, and mobility support
Identify and discuss available veterans' benefits and community resources
Document findings and determine appropriate follow-up actions

mismatches.patientClaim: Clarence describes the nephew's financial control as a longstanding, seemingly benign arrangement ('Dale handles the money now... said it'd be easier that way').
mismatches.recordEvidence: The prior social work note from 6 months ago documents that the patient 'reports managing independently, nephew assists with errands' with no concerns noted about finances at that time.
mismatches.teachingPoint: A prior assessment finding 'no concerns' does not rule out exploitation developing or escalating since - and may reflect under-disclosure at that time rather than true absence of risk. Longitudinal reassessment and trust-building are essential.

mismatches.patientClaim: Clarence states he takes his pain pill and blood pressure pill regularly and believes he is 'about out' of his cholesterol medicine, implying recent use.
mismatches.recordEvidence: The medication list shows the atorvastatin refill is 45 days overdue, while the other two medications were refilled on schedule 6 days ago - indicating he has likely been without the cholesterol medication for an extended period, longer than his own account suggests.
mismatches.teachingPoint: Patient self-report of medication adherence can be inaccurate or optimistic; cross-checking refill history reveals gaps that may need to be flagged to the medical team, even though medication management itself is outside social work's direct scope.

profile.title: Financial Exploitation, Self-Neglect, and Suicide Risk in an Isolated Older Veteran After a Fall
profile.summary: A social work student conducts a telehealth psychosocial follow-up with a 79-year-old veteran one week after discharge for fall-related rib fractures, uncovering suspected financial exploitation by a nephew, self-neglect (inadequate heat, food insecurity), moderate depression with passive suicidal ideation and firearm access, despite intact decision-making capacity. The case teaches trauma-informed interviewing to build trust, suicide risk and means-safety assessment, mandated APS reporting obligations that persist even when capacity is intact, and appropriate veteran-specific resource navigation within social work scope.
profile.setting: Telehealth video visit; patient at home in a single-wide trailer outside Beckley, West Virginia
